claims.text: 3D ink extrusion printing combined with hydrogen de-binding and titanium-sponge-gettered vacuum sintering produces a refined microstructure in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The combined processing route reduces residual oxygen in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The combined processing route lowers porosity.
A refined, lower-porosity microstructure and reduced residual oxygen support formation of a coherent protective oxide layer.
Titanium gettering removes excess oxygen during hydrogen de-binding and vacuum sintering.
3D ink extrusion provides improved control over microstructural features.
The processing-induced microstructure and oxygen reduction facilitate formation of a stable, slowly growing protective oxide.
The protective scale is likely to be alumina or another stable oxide.
A stable, slowly growing protective oxide minimizes oxygen ingress at high temperature.
Conventionally processed refractory high-entropy alloys typically have higher residual oxygen levels and less controlled microstructures than alloys made by the proposed route.
Higher residual oxygen and less controlled microstructure lead to faster high-temperature oxidation.
Relative to conventional processing, the proposed route will reduce oxidation-induced mass gain during exposure at approximately 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for about 50 hours.
Relative to conventional processing, the proposed route will improve oxide-scale integrity under the specified exposure.
Relative to conventional processing, the proposed route will improve retention of mechanical properties after the specified high-temperature exposure.
The proposed comparison uses conventionally processed samples as the control and exposes both groups at 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 50 hours.
Oxidation mass gain, oxide-scale morphology and integrity, and post-exposure mechanical properties will be measured.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement, exemplified by at least a 20% reduction in oxidation mass gain or demonstrably superior oxide-scale characteristics, will falsify the hypothesis.
